messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity incident detected — multiple serving-runtime pods reporting CUDA illegal memory access + OOM on gpu-pool-west.
incident-bot: Affected service: inference-runtime-v2. Estimated impact: 8% of requests failing with 500; elevated latencies. Auto-escalation triggered.
john: Oncall here. I'm looking at the alert groups. Which nodes are flapping?
sre-oncall: Nodes: gpu-west-12, gpu-west-14, gpu-west-19. Symptoms: repeated container restarts, kernel messages show 'WD: cuda: illegal device address' and pagewalk faults. Logs attached below.
john: Pasting relevant dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 1203.456789] python[23456]: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000128
[ 1203.456792] RIP: 0010:0x7f9c4c2a1234
[ 1203.456795] Code: … rgp_kernel+0x11f/0x200
[ 1203.456797] NIP:  [<0x7f9c4c2a1234>]  
[ 1203.456800] Bad address in kernel read from 0x0000000000000128
```
maria: Noted. We also see nvdriver warnings in pod logs: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" every ~30s after model reloads. Could be a race during KV cache warmup or a kernel regression.
carla: Any recent rollout of runtime or kernel patches to that pool in the last 24h?
ops-lead: We rolled runtime v2.3.7 to gpu-west last night. No kernel updates. v2.3.7 included a change to the loader that does async mmap + prefetch. Might be related.
eng-runtime: Agree suspect async mmap sequence. @john can you run `kubectl logs` for one of the failing pods and grep for the segfault stack?
john: Running now. Key stack snippet from runtime:
```
runtime_loader.cpp:load_segment() +0x3c
kvm_prefetcher.cpp:prefetch_async() +0x88
cuda_executor.cpp:launch_kernel() +0x11
```
john: Also saw a pattern where OOM occurs shortly after a reload sequence. Looks nondeterministic but correlated with concurrent requests during rollout.
maria: Immediate mitigation: let's cordon gpu-west-19 and drain it gracefully. Put node into maintenance to stop scheduling. Then rollback runtime to v2.3.6 on the remaining nodes in the pool.
carla: Ack. Initiating cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-west-19` and drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`.
ops-lead: Also toggle fallback routing: route tier-1 traffic to fallback-models in us-east for next 30m. Update routing policy in control plane.
eng-runtime: We should also disable async mmap prefetch flag on the runtime without full rollback as a faster mitigation: set ENV RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0 in deployment and roll.
john: Preparing a canary with RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0 on two nodes. If stable for 5 minutes, expand.
incident-bot: NOTE: Customer-facing impact detected. 12 customers with >1% errors, top affected: acme-inc (11%), mailhero (6%).
carla: I'll draft a quick customer blip to send to status page and affected customers. Concise: "We are investigating increased 500 errors and latency for inference-runtime in us-west. Engineers are mitigating; routing and rollbacks in progress. We will update in 30 minutes." Any objections?
maria: Fine. Send now.
carla: Posting status update to status.redwood.com/incidents/4829 and DMing account leads.
eng-runtime: Canary logs from RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0 pods show no CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS for ~7 minutes and stable memory footprint.
john: After expanding the flag-off rollout across gpu-west, node restarts stopped on the updated nodes. Nodes still flapping: gpu-west-12 (has older runtime), it's being drained now.
ops-lead: We're seeing 30% reduction in errors overall after rollout. Latency back to baseline for most customers. Keeping elevated monitoring for 60 more minutes.
maria: Root cause hypothesis: regression in async prefetch path under concurrent KV-cache warmup leading to a race in mmap/prefetch that triggers illegal device address access in driver. Potentially exposes a kernel null/dangling pointer in loader shim when mmappings race with CUDA pinning.
eng-runtime: Agree. Next steps: create a reproducer, add additional checks around mmap/prefetch ordering, and file a kernel/driver issue if we can isolate a dangling pointer. I'll open GH issue and link dmesg + reproducer.
john: Action items:
- john: finish draining remaining affected nodes and verify cluster stability (ETA 15m).
- eng-runtime: open reproducer issue + PR to disable prefetch by default (ETA 2d).
- ops-lead: keep fallback routing for 30m and monitor (ETA 1h).
- carla: customer comms update in 30m and postmortem draft (ETA 4h).
- maria: escalate to infra-sre if nodes show kernel panics after rollback (ETA immediate if observed).
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Error rate dropped from 8% -> 2% after targeted rollback/flag disable. No wider customer-impacting outages.
carla: Thanks team. Will keep channel open for updates. If anyone hits a regression after rollout, ping @sre-oncall and @eng-runtime.
john: Closing cordon on drained nodes after restart verification. Will post final status once all nodes stable.
eng-runtime: Linking GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/issues/914 — includes kernel logs, stack trace, and test harness.
carla: Final status for status page: "Mitigation: We rolled back a recent runtime change and disabled async prefetch on affected nodes. Error rates have substantially decreased. Engineers continue to investigate root cause; no ongoing customer-impacting failures." Publish?
maria: Publish. And add note: "If you observed persistent errors, contact support with request id examples." :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Monitoring window completed. Keep channel for postmortem comments.
